name: Question 2
worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. 

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=4x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(2{x}^{2})(-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2})-\int (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2})(4x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+2\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
